passage: On Monday, Salma clutched her toy giraffe while Hansa asked to hold it, and would not let go. On Tuesday she said, "Let's play shop. I am the shopkeeper and you are the customer. You borrow the giraffe and bring it back at closing time." She nodded to herself. "Customers always bring things back." Hansa borrowed it and gave it back when Salma rang the bell. On Thursday Hansa asked again, and Salma said, "Come to my shop," and handed the giraffe over at once.

qa.q: When was the giraffe to be brought back?
qa.a: The giraffe was to be brought back at closing time.

qa.q: What was Salma feeling on Monday when she clutched the giraffe and would not let go?
qa.a: Salma was worried about losing the giraffe or having it changed. Holding on tight shows she did not feel safe giving it up.

qa.q: What other approach could help Salma feel safe sharing, and why?
qa.a: She could ask a grown-up to set a timer for each turn. A timer promises the giraffe comes back.

qa.q: How does the game look to Hansa?
qa.a: Hansa is a customer who gets a turn with the giraffe and hands it back at closing. It is play, so Hansa gives it back happily.

grounding: A child turns sharing into a shop game where the other child borrows the toy and returns it at closing time.
